title: Data and patterns
objective: By the end of this lesson, you will be able to explain what data is, find a simple pattern in it, and say why a pattern from too little data can mislead.

sections.title: What is data?
sections.text: Data is information that has been collected and written down, such as test scores, temperatures, or the words in a message. AI systems learn from data, so the data they see shapes what they learn.

sections.title: Finding a pattern
sections.text: A pattern is something that repeats or changes in a regular way. In 2, 4, 6, 8 each number is 2 more than the one before. Once you see the pattern you can guess the next number. AI systems look for patterns like this, but in much larger and messier data.

sections.title: Summarising with an average
sections.text: An average (or mean) is one number that describes a whole list. Add the numbers up, then divide by how many there are. It is a simple way to see what is typical in a set of data.

sections.title: Too little data can mislead
sections.text: A pattern from only a few examples may be a coincidence. If it rained on your two birthdays, that does not mean it always rains on your birthday. More examples, and a wider mix of examples, give patterns you can trust more.

examples.title: Example 1: The average of some scores
examples.code:
scores = [3, 5, 4, 5, 5, 2]
total = 0
for s in scores:
    total = total + s
print(total / len(scores))

examples.title: Example 2: Predicting the next number
examples.code:
numbers = [2, 4, 6, 8]
step = numbers[1] - numbers[0]
print(numbers[-1] + step)

check_questions.prompt: You see that the bus was late on two days in a row. What is the best thing to say?
options: Two days is too few to be sure, so keep collecting data
The bus will be on time from now on
check_questions.explanation: A pattern from two examples may be a coincidence. Collect more data before trusting it.

misconception.0: Two examples are not enough to say always.
misconception.2: Two examples cannot promise what happens next.
misconception.3: Data can help, but only when there is enough of it.
